Deputy Director, Facilities Operations

Santa Clara County

Post Date

August 17, 2026

Description

We are seeking a dynamic, future focused leader to serve as the Deputy Director, Facilities Operations, overseeing the facility operations and infrastructure planning of Valley Medical Center and Regional Medical Center, two of the system’s most complex and essential hospitals. This is a rare opportunity to modernize a highly technical, mission critical environment and ensure that our facilities remain safe, resilient, and fully operational to support exceptional patient care.

Your Mission

Lead operational excellence, innovation, and long-range planning for facilities operations across the County’s diverse and mission-critical environments. In this leadership role, you will ensure facilities are safe, resilient, sustainable, and fully aligned with the County’s strategic priorities and community commitments.

What Makes This Role Unique

Scale, Diversity, and Complexity: The County’s facilities portfolio spans hospitals, outpatient clinics, laboratories, administrative buildings, and multiple 24-hour operational environments. In this role, you will oversee an exceptionally broad and complex network of facilities and guide multidisciplinary teams across engineering, building systems, maintenance, environmental services, biomed engineering, telecom, low-voltage infrastructure, and more.
Healthcare-Centered Scope: As part of one of California’s largest public healthcare systems, this role oversees operations in highly regulated, high-acuity environments where safety and reliability directly support patient care. You will work at the intersection of healthcare delivery and infrastructure stewardship, ensuring that critical hospital and clinical settings operate seamlessly around the clock.
Strategic Executive Partnership: The position plays a pivotal role in shaping the County’s long-range facilities strategy. You will develop executive-level recommendations and help inform infrastructure investments that impact the daily lives of millions of residents. Your insights will influence decisions that define the County’s operational capabilities for years to come.
Commitment to Equity and Community: Every facility under your responsibility will serve a community that depends on reliable, safe, and accessible public services. The role directly supports the County’s broader mission to advance equity, enhance access to care, and uphold the wellbeing of residents who rely on County hospitals, clinics, and essential services.

What You Bring

Extensive facilities management experience in a large, complex public, or healthcare organization.
Demonstrated leadership overseeing engineering, trades, and technical support teams.
Strong background in healthcare facilities, including regulatory compliance, safety, and technical systems.
Proven success working in unionized environments.
Expertise in budgeting, forecasting, asset management, and capital planning.
Ability to build trust with leadership, staff, clinicians, and stakeholders.

jobs.description:
Why Join The Drata Team?

The best way to understand the Driver’s Mindset is to see it in action. We’re an award-winning, mission-driven team of 600+ people worldwide
, united by a culture that values trust, speed, and continuous growth.

Hear the Voice of the Team: Explore our "Life at Drata" page for employee testimonials on our collaborative and the growth opportunities available.
Connect with Us on Socials: LinkedIn - follow us for company updates, employee stories, and career news.

Job Summary

As Drata scales, we're looking for a strategic, operationally stellar Sr. Executive Business Partner to support our CEO & Co-Founder. This role sits at the heart of Drata's operational engine: translating vision into action, keeping the executive team and internal teams aligned, and giving our CEO the space to lead with clarity and momentum.

You'll thrive here if you lead with relationships, build trust quickly with everyone from the executive team to board members and investors, and don't take yourself too seriously even when the pace picks up. The CEO's office moves fast and deals with a lot of ambiguity, so we're looking for someone comfortable making calls with incomplete information, adapting as priorities shift, and pulling people together rather than working in isolation. We're also looking for genuine enthusiasm about where AI is headed and how it can reshape executive operations; someone excited to bring new AI tools into the day-to-day of the CEO's office, not just tolerate them.

What You'll Do

Strategic Leadership & Executive Support

Partner directly with the CEO to advance strategic initiatives, assess risks, and keep priorities aligned with Drata's mission and growth objectives.
Anticipate leadership needs and proactively remove barriers to enable fast, informed decisions.
Prioritize and manage critical issues, surfacing the information that guides executive action.
Prepare data-backed briefings, presentations, and materials for executive, internal, and investor meetings.
Facilitate clear communication between the CEO, executive team, and external stakeholders.

Operational Leadership & Business Continuity

Manage day-to-day operations of the CEO's office, keeping decision-making, prioritization, and problem-solving on track.
Act as the CEO's trusted proxy during key periods or transitions.
Partner with Finance and Legal on the CEO's office budget, approvals, and resource allocation, using automation where it helps.
Support planning and execution of leadership offsites, company all-hands, and other high-visibility moments.

Organizational Performance & Strategic Execution

Design and implement work plans that move the needle on company-wide goals.
Support the creation, tracking, and analysis of company OKRs and KPIs with the executive team.
Monitor milestones across departments and recommend course corrections to optimize outcomes.
Lead or support special projects, including M&A, reorganizations, and cross-functional automation efforts, from discovery to execution.
Support headcount planning, org design, and onboarding programs with the People team.
Own the agenda for executive staff meetings and track completion of pre-work.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Collaboration

Act as a strategic connector across teams, translating executive priorities into coordinated action.
Structure leadership meetings, offsites, and planning sessions to build shared vision and outcomes.
Meet regularly with cross-functional leaders to keep everyone aligned on the CEO's goals and OKRs.
Maintain an active pulse on the State of the State; bringing actionable information and insights to the CEO in a timely manner.

Data, Reporting & Continuous Improvement

Oversee performance reporting and data insights that support executive decision-making.
Use tools like Slack Workflows, Zapier, and other automation platforms to streamline operations.
Champion continuous improvement and change management efforts across the organization.

Communication & Stakeholder Management

Draft and coordinate internal and external communications on behalf of the CEO, including company-wide updates.
Ghostwrite executive communications and craft strategic messaging in the CEO's voice.
Serve as a liaison for investors, board members, customers, and press/analysts as needed.
Identify and escalate communication gaps quickly.

Executive Office Management & Travel

Manage the CEO's calendar with precision, balancing meeting priorities with travel and high-impact events.
Handle timely submission of the CEO's expenses and track related spend.
Some travel required for board meetings, investor events, and leadership offsites, including to Drata's San Francisco HQ.

What You'll Bring

High emotional intelligence, resilience, sound judgment, and a sense of humor.
A warm, energizing relationship-builder who earns trust quickly with the CEO, executive team, board members, and investors alike, and keeps teams aligned amid ambiguity or shifting priorities.
8+ years of executive support experience in a SaaS or high-growth startup environment, including direct experience supporting a CEO or other C-level executive.
4+ years of leadership experience managing business operations or executive support programs across multiple functions and time zones.
Experience supporting board and investor relations with a high degree of discretion and professionalism.
Expertise building and scaling operational frameworks, including OKRs, org planning, and SOPs, for a high-growth organization.
A track record leading cross-functional initiatives, including M&A, reorganizations, and automation implementations.
Outstanding written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to ghostwrite executive communications and craft strategic messaging.
Tech-savvy, with hands-on experience using tools like Slack, Zapier, Claude, ChatGPT, or Glean to work faster and smarter.
Passion for GRC, cybersecurity, compliance, and Drata's mission to build trust across the internet.

How We Support You

At Drata, our people are our strongest advantage—and we prove it with support that exceeds industry standards. Our total rewards package is designed to power your well-being, accelerate your growth, and keep your work-life balance thriving.

Explore how we invest in your Life at Drata.

Shared Success: We provide stock equity to ensure that as the company grows, you share directly in that success. Equity gives every employee a sense of ownership and the opportunity to celebrate our wins together—because your contributions don’t just support our progress; they help drive our collective success.
Health & Wellness: Up to 100% employer-paid premiums for medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and their dependents, along with comprehensive wellness benefits and healthcare concierge services designed to support your needs beyond traditional insurance.
Financial Well-being: A comprehensive suite of financial benefits, including a 401(k) plan, company-paid life and disability insurance, tax-advantaged spending accounts, and a range of discounted voluntary offerings to help you customize and strengthen your overall financial position.
Family Support: We want to support you in life's most important moments, so we offer a paid Parental Leave policy, after six months of employment. Employees also receive access to Kindbody fertility and family-building benefits and dedicated leave specialists who help guide you through the entire process.
Growth & Development: Generous annual stipends for both professional and personal development, empowering you to invest in your continued growth. You’ll also have access to a wide range of internal learning opportunities, ensuring you can build new skills, deepen your expertise, and advance your career with confidence.
Time Off & Flexibility: We believe that to do your best work, you should get the time you need for rest, rejuvenation and recovery. Drata offers a flexible vacation policy, paid holidays, and other perks to recharge.

The expected base salary range for this role is between $150,000 - $230,000 and is listed to provide transparency. Actual base pay will vary based on multiple factors — market location, job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and overall alignment to the role. Candidates shouldn't expect automatic placement at any particular point within the range. Offer amounts are determined by the qualifications each candidate brings to the position. Total compensation may also include equity designed to provide meaningful ownership in the company, as well as health and wellbeing benefits.

Senior Director of Operations

Join Our “Relationships-First” Team

We invite you to be a part of a team whose mission-aligned culture offers sustainable, rewarding career paths in teaching, operations, and leadership, built on collaboration and mutual support. Experience the difference at a workplace that celebrates and cultivates each team member’s passions, skills and multi-disciplinary interests as we build a brighter future together, one student at a time.

Why Educators Choose S2

A “Relationships-First” culture where you’re valued, supported, and included
Collaborative planning time and mutual support
Opportunities to lead initiatives that strengthen student growth at every stage of their PreK–12 education

About The Senior Director Of Operations

The Senior Director of Operations is a key member of the Operations team, reporting to the Chief Operating Officer. This role owns the day-to-day systems that let teachers and principals focus on instruction: school operations across all four campuses, legal and regulatory compliance, afterschool programming, and enrollment. The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, comfortable managing multiple workstreams at once, and skilled at building systems and relationships that hold up under a fast-paced, growing school network.

Responsibilities

Lead Operational Excellence

Champion operational excellence across S2's four campuses by building systems that allow students, teachers, and leaders to focus on exceptional teaching and learning.
Establish operational standards and continuously improve facilities, safety, food service, transportation, and campus operations.
Build strong vendor partnerships and hold service providers accountable for quality, responsiveness, and fiscal stewardship.
Lead long-term operational planning, including space utilization, capital projects, and infrastructure improvements.

Drive Organizational Compliance and Risk Management

Foster a culture of compliance that ensures S2 consistently meets city, state, federal, and charter requirements.
Develop systems that proactively manage compliance risks and strengthen organizational accountability.
Oversee regulatory reporting, audits, and documentation with accuracy and timeliness.
Partner with the Chief Operating Officer and legal counsel to oversee contracts, insurance, and organizational risk.
Strengthen policies, procedures, and internal controls to support organizational growth.

Lead High-Quality Early Childhood Compliance

Ensure S2's Pre-K program meets all health and regulatory requirements while maintaining a safe learning environment.
Lead the annual recertification process and build systems that support ongoing compliance.

Shape Exceptional Afterschool and Summer Programming

Lead the strategy and operations for afterschool and summer programs that provide safe, engaging student experiences.
Manage external partnerships and ensure high standards for quality and accountability.
Use enrollment and family feedback to strengthen programming and expand access.
Ensure all programs meet licensing, health, safety, and operational requirements.

Lead Enrollment Strategy and Community Engagement

Lead the network-wide enrollment strategy from recruitment through re-enrollment with excellence and compliance.
Develop systems that support enrollment growth while meeting New York State charter requirements.
Partner with school leaders and the Family Support team to strengthen community outreach.
Analyze enrollment data to inform staffing, budgeting, and long-term planning.
Build strong relationships with families and community partners that support enrollment and trust.

Build Systems, Develop Others, And Lead Through Influence

Build strong cross-campus partnerships and align teams around shared operational goals.
Design systems that improve efficiency, consistency, and organizational scalability.
Coach and develop team members through clear expectations, feedback, and accountability.
Serve as a strategic thought partner to the Chief Operating Officer and school leaders.
Model S2's Relationships First philosophy through integrity, collaboration, and service.

Who You Are

Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree preferred
Minimum of five years of professional experience, including at least two years managing operations, compliance, or programmatic functions, ideally in a school or nonprofit setting

Skilled at building organizational processes and systems that hold up as an organization scales

At S2, we take as much care of our staff as we do of our students. All of our faculty and staff are valued professionals and we are proud to provide team-building and collaboration, comfortable and friendly working conditions and more, to ensure our team members have the tools they need to succeed.

In addition to meaningful and rewarding work, S2 provides competitive salaries, an excellent benefits package, a 401K program with an organizational match, longevity bonus, generous paid time off, access to a federal student loan debt reduction program, and a friendly work environment. Additionally, we provide opportunities for supplemental compensation, an excellent benefits package with

a 401K program with a 6% organizational match

A subsidiary of the Metropolitan Transportation Authority, Metro-North Railroad is one of the busiest commuter railroads in the nation. MTA Metro-North Railroad strives to provide a safe and reliable commute, excellent customer service, and rewarding opportunities for its employees.

Metro-North Railroad reserves the right to remove this posting before the Application Deadline.

Direct and control Metro-North Signal Force Account resources (labor, material, equipment and systems) to effect safe, economical and efficient installation and revisions to wayside signal and PTC infrastructure on the New Haven, Harlem & Hudson and West of Hudson line territories in support of Metro-North Railroad's Five -year Signal Capital Program, third party projects and other Five-year capital programs. Primarily focusing on the Signal Construction Group.

Provide leadership and direction to Signal Construction management staff, supervisory personnel and agreement forces in the safe and efficient execution of the wayside signal and PTC system installations and system modifications.
Plan and control wayside infrastructure installation schedules, resource allocation and system commissioning practices and procedures. Review, document and monitor, signal testing and preventative maintenance practices during installation and cutover of systems.
Evaluate construction practices, materials and staging techniques for wayside signal systems and select the most efficient and economical method for each project or system upgrade.
Develop project and system costs estimates and schedules necessary to support wayside installations and modifications.

Provide a lead in supporting Metro-North Safety Program through the execution of required activities and policies associated with personnel working along or on the railroad right-of-way. Active participation in ECR, DSAP and other safety and practice review and inspections.
Select, develop, and motivate staff and provide career development for team members. Provide effective coaching and counseling. Manage team and individual performance. Create a professional environment that respects individual differences and enables staff to develop and contribute to their full potential.

Strong oral and written communication skills.

Chief Program Officer

Bonneville Environmental Foundation (BEF) is an entrepreneurial nonprofit working on environmental solutions at the intersection of renewable energy and freshwater. Partnerships are key to our success. We build long-term relationships with our corporate, utility, non-profit, and philanthropic partners by understanding their goals and needs and providing solutions that achieve those goals while delivering real, measurable environmental benefits.

Who are we looking for?

BEF is seeking an experienced, mission-driven executive to serve as its first Chief Program Officer (CPO). Reporting to the CEO and serving alongside the CFO and Chief of Staff, the CPO will provide integrated leadership across BEF's full portfolio of water, carbon, and energy programs. This is a newly created role that reflects BEF's ambitions for expanded impact and the increasing complexity of its program work. The CPO will contribute to and hold center on program performance; drive and manage strategic growth in emerging program areas (for example water and energy stewardship for the data center sector); expand BEF's client base and revenue streams to reduce revenue concentration risk; and support meaningful program partnerships that support priorities of Tribal Nations. The ideal candidate brings deep experience managing (and directly supporting the success of) complex program portfolios in a mission-driven organization; a rigorous approach to performance management; and a genuine commitment to equity, partnership, and impact.

Why Join Us? Our Values Are:

Partnership: We believe we can accomplish more by working together.
Adaptability: We evolve, adapt, and apply what we learn to improve our approaches and outcomes.
Knowledge: We seek out and value diverse perspectives, embrace new ideas, and advance new approaches.
Innovation: We recognize that the scope and pace of the change we need demands innovation, drawing on knowledge from the past and new information and tools.
Integrity: We are honest with our employees, customers, and our partners. We seek to deliver outcomes that benefit the environment and people we serve.

Primary Duties:

Program Leadership and Integration (A Strategic Leader)

Provide executive oversight, vision, and cohesion across BEF's full portfolio of water, carbon, and energy programs, ensuring alignment and synergy with organizational mission and strategic priorities.
Serve as the primary senior leader for Program Directors and Senior Directors, setting a high standard for program quality, staff development, innovation and adaptation, and cross-team collaboration.
Take responsibility for, and directly contribute to, sustained program performance.
Review, synthesize, and track results across program portfolios, and translate them into actionable guidance and strategic adaptation for program teams and executive leadership.
Identify and resolve structural, operational, or resourcing barriers that inhibit program effectiveness, growth, and mission impact.

Performance Management and Accountability (A Rigorous Performance Manager)

Develop and maintain a rigorous, organization-wide framework for program metrics, key performance indicators, and impact measurement.
Hold the organization and program teams accountable for delivering impact and value to partners while fostering a culture of learning, continuous improvement, and a supportive atmosphere.

The Moran Company is pleased to partner with The Arc Connecticut to recruit the organization's Executive Director.

The Arc Connecticut is an advocacy organization committed to protecting the rights of individuals with Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities (I/DD) and promoting opportunities for their full inclusion in their communities. The organization is the statewide chapter affiliated with The Arc of the United States, the nation’s oldest and largest non-profit federation advocating for and supporting people with I/DD and their families since 1950. The Arc Connecticut is an independent 501(c)(3) corporation established in Connecticut over 60 years ago. As the state chapter, The Arc convenes and supports 13 other Arc chapters (independent corporations) with total combined revenue of over $111 million, more than 170 board members, over 4,000 staff, and over 1,800 volunteers.

The Arc Connecticut has grown and adapted to the changes that people with disabilities face across their life span. Through the decades, The Arc has seen several name changes, advocated for the passage of state legislation on behalf of people with disabilities, assisted in the creation of and advocated for the private provider system of support, filed 4 class action lawsuits, advocated for the closure of institutions, and continued to advocate for individuals with I/DD and their families.

The work today is illustrated by The Arc Connecticut Family Network (formerly Families for Families), created in 2012 to give families a united voice — within the Department of Developmental Services (DDS), at the Capitol, and across their local communities. The network brings families together to share information, collaborate on local and statewide issues, and connect directly with lawmakers and Connecticut’s federal delegation under the leadership of the Director of Advocacy.

The organization advances its public policy priorities through an annual legislative agenda, supported by family and advocate education, network growth, legislative outreach, relationship-building, coalitions, and partnerships.

The Arc Connecticut is governed by a volunteer board of 16, led by two staff members (including the Executive Director), and supported by annual revenue of $450,000 generated by chapter dues and fundraising. In addition, efforts are amplified through contracts with marketing/public relations consultants and a governmental affairs consultant. The Executive Director position is based within the state of Connecticut, and duties are performed remotely.

The Executive Director serves as the chief executive officer of The Arc Connecticut, leading statewide advocacy and policy efforts while overseeing operations, supporting local chapters, implementing strategic plans, and building relationships with key stakeholders. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the ideal candidate will be an outgoing, visionary, and analytical leader with fundraising experience and knowledge of, or the ability to learn, the funding and service-delivery systems for people with I/DD.

The Executive Director will serve as the organization’s primary spokesperson and advocate, advancing policies, programs, and services that benefit individuals with I/DD and their families. This leader will develop and implement the organization’s policy and strategic agendas, monitor legislative and regulatory developments, build coalitions, and represent The Arc Connecticut in public policy forums. The Executive Director will support local chapters by providing guidance, training, resources, and opportunities for collaboration while incorporating their priorities into statewide efforts. Responsibilities also include overseeing daily operations, staff, finances, compliance, fundraising, community engagement, and organizational effectiveness. In partnership with the Board of Directors, the Executive Director will establish priorities, report on organizational performance, and support the Board’s governance, fiduciary, and strategic responsibilities.

The successful candidate will be a Connecticut resident with at least five years of progressively responsible leadership experience in the social or human services sector, a bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience, strong communication skills, and demonstrated fundraising expertise. Preferred qualifications include knowledge of services and advocacy for individuals with I/DD, experience in community organizing and working with governing boards, and the ability to use technology to improve operations, fundraising, and support services. The position requires 25% (up to 50% at certain times), mostly in-state day travel.

The annual salary for this position is expected to be in the $100,000 range, commensurate with the background and experience of the selected candidate. The Arc currently provides paid leave, a stipend for individual health coverage, and contributions to an IRA.

Position Summary

The College of Business at MSU Denver seeks a forward-thinking, visionary, and experienced leader to serve as the next Executive Director of the FHLBank Topeka Affordable Housing Institute. The Executive Director of the FHLBank Topeka Affordable Housing Institute (AHI) provides strategic leadership, operational oversight, and academic integration for MSU Denver’s interdisciplinary affordable housing initiative. This is a 12-month appointment with ongoing, year-round administrative and instructional duties reporting to the Chair of the Department of Finance.

The Executive Director of the FHLBank Topeka Affordable Housing Institute serves as the academic, strategic, and community-facing leader for affordable housing education, workforce development, industry engagement, non-credit programming, and interdisciplinary academic integration. Housed within the College of Business and connected to the Department of Finance, the Institute supports students, faculty, community partners, housing professionals, developers, financial institutions, nonprofit organizations, public agencies, and industry stakeholders by connecting affordable housing knowledge with education, career pathways, applied learning, and community impact.

The Executive Director is responsible for advancing the Institute’s role as a regional leader in affordable housing education and workforce development. The Executive Director will help position MSU Denver as a distinctive public urban university partner for affordable housing finance, policy, development, management, and community-centered housing solutions. The Executive Director will also support student success, professional mobility, and industry engagement by helping students and working professionals develop the knowledge, skills, experiences, and relationships needed to contribute to the affordable housing sector. The Executive Director will work closely with faculty, college leadership, University Advancement, C2 Hub, the Affordable Housing Industry Navigator, the AHI Advisory Council, and external stakeholders.

Fundraising & Advancement

Partner with University Advancement to secure grants, sponsorships, and philanthropic support
Prepare proposals, manage funded projects, and ensure reporting compliance

Convene events such as summits, panels, and practitioner workshops

Non-Credit Program Development

Lead development and delivery of non-credit programs (certificates, workshops, executive education)
Recruit instructors and ensure program quality
Track outcomes and align offerings with workforce needs

Advisory Council & Stakeholder Engagement

Represent AHI to internal and external stakeholders

Position the Institute as a distinctive regional leader in affordable housing education, industry-connected learning, workforce development, and community impact.

Instruction, Curriculum Innovation, and Industry Alignment (40%)

Collaborate with faculty to align non-credit programming with academic pathways

Participate as a contributing member of the Department of Finance faculty community, including coordination and program support as needed

Contribute to assurance of learning (AoL) and accreditation-related activities as needed

Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills

Experience integrating industry practice with curriculum development, student learning, experiential education, or career-connected programming
Knowledge of affordable housing finance, policy, development, management, real estate, public-private partnerships, community development, or housing-related workforce needs

Founded in New Mexico, Securin was built on the belief that effective security shouldn’t depend on unlimited budgets or perfect conditions. Our team brings deep experience in offensive security, vulnerability research, and hands-on incident response, including advising state and federal agencies, schools, hospitals, utilities, and critical infrastructure organizations.

Partner with technical and product teams to translate complex cybersecurity concepts into compelling, accessible narratives
Develop executive thought leadership content including LinkedIn articles, conference presentations, and speaking submissions
